research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator, Home Office and GOV.UK primary guidance only; enforcement and Fire Safety (England) Regulations methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Revised fire-door scope
verified_claims: The revised 2025 guidance clarifies that regulation 10 is not intended to require existing flat entrance doors to meet current new-build door standards.
limitations: The clarification does not excuse inadequate doors or defects identified by a fire-risk assessment.

sources.name: Existing-door adequacy
verified_claims: A door that met the relevant standard when the block or door was built may remain adequate if it is undamaged and gaps are not excessive.
limitations: Age or original compliance alone does not prove present adequacy.

sources.name: Certification and seal absence
verified_claims: Absence of certification, intumescent strips or smoke seals does not by itself mean an existing door is unfit for purpose.
limitations: Their absence must still be considered with the fire-risk assessment, door design and condition.

sources.name: Regulation 10 building scope
verified_claims: Regulation 10 applies to blocks containing at least two domestic premises and common parts used for evacuation, including purpose-built and converted blocks.
limitations: The rule does not establish whether a named property meets the statutory premises definition.

sources.name: Responsible-person communal duty
verified_claims: The responsible person for communal parts is responsible for arranging the checks required by the regulations.
limitations: The guidance does not identify the responsible person for a specific ownership or management structure.

sources.name: Fire-door information for all residents
verified_claims: Information about flat entrance doors must be provided to residents in all blocks within regulation 10's scope.
limitations: Providing information is not evidence that doors have been inspected or repaired.

sources.name: Fire-door routine-check height threshold
verified_claims: Routine regulation 10 checks apply where the building's top storey is more than 11 metres above ground level.
limitations: Height and storey status require building-specific measurement.

sources.name: Fire-risk assessment prerequisite
verified_claims: A suitable and sufficient fire-risk assessment should identify relevant doors and assess whether they adequately resist fire and smoke.
limitations: A fire-risk assessment record does not prove that its findings remain current or implemented.

sources.name: Competent fire-door repair
verified_claims: Where a door is inadequate or needs repair or replacement, the work must be undertaken by a competent person or contractor.
limitations: A contractor's appointment or certificate does not prove that every defect was properly corrected.

sources.name: Resident fire-door behaviour
verified_claims: Residents must be told to keep fire doors shut, not tamper with self-closing devices and report faults or damage immediately.
limitations: Resident information does not establish actual resident behaviour or door condition.

sources.name: Move-in and annual fire-door reminders
verified_claims: Fire-door information must be provided to new residents as soon as reasonably practicable and repeated at intervals not exceeding 12 months.
limitations: A distribution schedule does not prove that every resident received or understood the information.

sources.name: Fire-door inspection frequency
verified_claims: For buildings above the threshold, flat entrance doors require best-endeavours checks at least annually and communal fire doors at least every three months.
limitations: Frequency compliance does not establish the adequacy or quality of each check.

sources.name: Simple visual fire-door checks
verified_claims: Regulation 10 checks are intended to be simple visual checks that generally do not require tools or a specialist.
limitations: Simple checks do not replace specialist assessment within the wider fire-risk-assessment process.

sources.name: Flat access and check records
verified_claims: Responsible persons should arrange access with residents and record steps taken, including cases where access was not granted.
limitations: Recorded attempts do not prove that a door was inspected or that legal action is justified.

sources.name: Door condition and self-closing checks
verified_claims: Checks should cover damage, glazing, hinges, seals where present, excessive gaps and effective full self-closing from different opening angles.
limitations: A visual pass does not establish certified fire resistance or future performance during a fire.
